This document is a reference card for every Normal-Block variant implemented in `src/` (C++/RcppArmadillo core) and validated against the R6 reference implementation. It follows the notation of @tousPhD2026 : $\odot$ Hadamard product, $\oslash$ term-to-term inverse, $A_i$ the (column) transpose of the $i$-th row of $A$, and

$$A_{\mathrm{row\text{-}sum}} = \Big(\sum_i A_{i\cdot}\Big)^\top, \qquad
A_{\mathrm{col\text{-}sum}} = \sum_j A_{\cdot j}, \qquad
A_{\mathrm{total\text{-}sum}} = \sum_{ij} A_{ij}.$$

For each variant we give: the generative model, the optimized criterion (log-likelihood or ELBO), and the explicit E/M (or VE/M) updates exactly as implemented in `src/`. All formulas below have been checked against @tousPhD2026, @tous2026 and @ngalala2026; the C++ recursions are tested against R reference implementations and against the exact log-likelihood where it is available (`tests/testthat/test-cpp-*.R`, `test-heldout-loglik.R`).

These models and their inference algorithms were developed over the PhD thesis of Jeanne Tous (Normal-Block family, §§0-9; @tousPhD2026, @tous2026) and the Master's research internship of Nestor Ngalala Manguitini (Mean-Block family, §§10-11; @ngalala2026), both supervised by Julien Chiquet. Jeanne Tous also participated in the supervision of Nestor's internship.

> **Note on the use of generative AI.** The models themselves -- their definition and every algebraic derivation -- were worked out by the students and their advisor over these two projects, who also wrote the first working versions of the code, its object-oriented architecture, and the first simulation studies. Generative AI (Claude Sonnet and Claude Opus, Anthropic) was used afterwards to improve the documentation (including this document), produce synthesis material, and audit, test, and improve the code -- in particular to port several algorithmic components to C++: the E/M and VE/M steps detailed below, their SQUAREM-accelerated variant (§18), and the graphical lasso solver (§17), whose original R-callback implementation caused intermittent memory crashes.

# Part I -- The models

This part is the mathematical reference: for each variant, the generative model, the criterion being optimized, and the explicit updates.

## Normal-Block models (variance clustering)

The clustering structures the *latent covariance*: two variables are in the same block when they respond identically to a shared latent factor, i.e. when they **covary** the same way (§§0-9). This is the model of @tousPhD2026 and @tous2026, and the one the package (and this document) are named after.

### 0. The generative model

$$\begin{aligned}
\text{Latent space:} \quad & W_i \sim \mathcal N(0, \Omega^{-1}), \quad W_i \in \mathbb R^q \\
\text{Observation space:} \quad & Y_i \mid W_i \sim \mathcal N(C W_i + B^\top X_i,\, D), \quad Y_i \in \mathbb R^p
\end{aligned}$$

$Y$ ($n\times p$), $X$ ($n\times d$), $W$ ($n\times q$, stacked row-wise). $C$ ($p\times q$) is either a fixed 0/1 clustering matrix (**known clusters**), or a matrix of $\mathrm{Mult}(1,\alpha)$ membership probabilities $\tau$ (**unknown clusters**, inferred jointly with everything else). $D$ is the residual covariance: $D = \mathrm{diag}(d^{-1})$ (**diagonal** noise) or $D = \xi^{-1} I_p$ (**spherical** noise, i.e. $d$ constant across variables).

**Within-block correlations are positive.** For $j\neq l$ in block $k$, $\mathrm{Cov}(Y_{ij}, Y_{il}\mid X_i) = \Sigma_{kk} > 0$ ($\Sigma = \Omega^{-1}$), so their correlation $\Sigma_{kk}/\sqrt{(\Sigma_{kk}+d_j^{-1})(\Sigma_{kk}+d_l^{-1})}$ lies in $(0,1)$, whatever the parameters: the members of a block are noisy copies of the same latent signal $W_{\cdot k}$, and two anticorrelated variables can only sit in different blocks, linked by a negative $\Sigma_{kl}$. `within_block_correlations()` checks this property on a fitted model (most useful for a known clustering).

### 1. Known clusters, diagonal noise (EM)

R6: `NormalBlockVarKnownClusters` (`noise_covariance = "diagonal"`).

C++: `norm_block_var_cov_diag_noise_known_clusters`.

**E-step.** Posterior $W_i \mid Y_i \sim \mathcal N(\mu_i, \Gamma)$, shared $\Gamma$ ($C$ is fixed, so $\Gamma$ does not depend on $i$):

$$\Gamma = (\Omega+ C^\top D^{-1} C)^{-1} \qquad [q \times q]$$

$$\mu = (Y - XB)\, D^{-1} C \Gamma \qquad [n \times q]$$

**M-step.** With $R_\mu = Y - XB - \mu C^\top$:

$$\hat B = (X^\top X)^{-1} X^\top (Y - \mu C^\top)$$

$$\hat\Sigma = \frac{1}{n}\mu^\top\mu + \Gamma$$

$$\hat\Omega= \hat\Sigma^{-1} \qquad \text{(or graphical lasso, §13)}$$

$$\hat d = \frac{(R_\mu^2)_{\mathrm{col\text{-}sum}}}{n} + C\,\mathrm{diag}(\Gamma)$$

**Criterion** (the exact marginal log-likelihood of $Y$, valid at *any* $(B,d,\Omega)$, not only at an M-step optimum -- $Y_i$ is marginally $\mathcal N(B^\top X_i, D + C\Omega^{-1}C^\top)$, and $|D+C\Omega^{-1}C^\top|$/$(D+C\Omega^{-1}C^\top)^{-1}$ are rewritten through $\Gamma^{-1}=\Omega+C^\top D^{-1}C$ -- the same $q\times q$ matrix the E-step above inverts -- via the matrix determinant lemma and the Woodbury identity, avoiding the $p\times p$ inverse entirely). With $R = Y-XB$ and $\mu$/$\Gamma$ as in the E-step (an identity valid for *any* $\theta$, since this model's E-step is exact Gaussian conditioning, not an approximation):

$$J = -\frac{np}{2}\log(2\pi) + \frac{n}{2}\sum_j \log(d_j) + \frac{n}{2}\log|\Omega| + \frac{n}{2}\log|\Gamma|
    - \frac12\Big(\underbrace{\textstyle\sum_j d_j\,(R^2)_{\mathrm{col\text{-}sum}_j}}_{\text{weighted SSQ}} - \mathrm{tr}(\Gamma^{-1}\mu^\top\mu)\Big)$$

> **On the relation to a simpler, M-step-only formula.** At a point where $d$ is exactly the M-step's own argmax for *this same* $\mu/\Gamma$ (i.e. right after a real E-step/M-step pair, as in plain EM -- but *not*, e.g., at a SQUAREM-extrapolated candidate), the bracketed quadratic term collapses to the constant $np$, and $J$ reduces to $-\frac{np}{2}\log(2\pi e) + \frac n2\sum_j\log(d_j) + \frac n2\log|\Omega| + \frac n2\log|\Gamma|$. The general form above is what `objective()` now actually computes, since it remains valid off that trajectory.

### 2. Known clusters, spherical noise (EM)

R6: `NormalBlockVarKnownClusters` (`noise_covariance = "spherical"`).

C++: `norm_block_var_cov_spherical_noise_known_clusters`.

Identical to §1 except $d$ is replaced by a single scalar $\xi$, shared across all $p$ variables:

$$\xi^{-1} = \frac{1}{p}\sum_j \hat d_j = \frac{(R_\mu^2)_{\mathrm{total\text{-}sum}}}{np} + \frac{C_{\mathrm{col\text{-}sum}}^\top \mathrm{diag}(\Gamma)}{p}$$

($\hat d$ as in §1, before collapsing to a scalar.) The criterion is the same formula as §1 with $d_j = \xi$ for all $j$ (so $\sum_j\log(d_j) = p\log(\xi)$, and the weighted SSQ collapses to $\xi\cdot(R^2)_{\mathrm{total\text{-}sum}}$).

### 3. Unknown clusters, diagonal noise (VEM)

R6: `NormalBlockVarUnknownClusters` (`noise_covariance = "diagonal"`).

C++: `norm_block_var_cov_diag_noise_unknown_clusters`.

Mean-field approximation $\mathbb P(W, C \mid Y) \approx \prod_i \pi_1(W_i) \prod_j \pi_2(C_j)$, with $W_i \sim \mathcal N(M_i, \mathrm{diag}(S))$ ($S$ shared across rows -- no zero-inflation mask to break that symmetry) and $C_j \sim \mathrm{Mult}(1, \tau_{j\cdot})$.

**VE-step.**

$$\tilde\Gamma = (\Omega+ \mathrm{diag}(\tau^\top d))^{-1} \qquad [q\times q,\ \text{shared}]$$

$$M = (Y - XB)\, D^{-1}\tau\tilde\Gamma \qquad [n\times q]$$

$$S = \mathrm{diag}(\tilde\Gamma) \qquad [q]$$

$$\eta = d \otimes_{\text{rows}} \big((Y-XB)^\top M\big) - \frac12\, d\, \big(M^2_{\mathrm{col\text{-}sum}} + nS\big)^\top
       + \mathbf 1_p \log(\alpha)^\top - 1$$

$$\tau_{j\cdot} = \mathrm{softmax}(\eta_{j\cdot}) \qquad \text{(skipped if } q=1 \text{ or fixed\_tau)}$$

**M-step.** With $R = Y - XB$ (computed at the *start* of the VEM iteration, refreshed once $B$ is updated below -- see Part II) and $A = R^2 - 2R\odot(M\tau^\top) + (M^2+S)\tau^\top$:

$$\hat B = (X^\top X)^{-1}X^\top(Y - M\tau^\top)$$

$$\hat d = \mathrm{mean}_{\text{rows}}(A)$$

$$\hat\Sigma_q = \frac{1}{n}M^\top M + \mathrm{diag}(S)$$

$$\hat\Omega= \hat\Sigma_q^{-1} \qquad \text{(or graphical lasso, §13)}$$

$$\hat\alpha = \mathrm{mean}_{\text{cols}}(\tau)$$

**Criterion** (ELBO):

$$J = -\frac{np}{2}\log(2\pi e) + \frac{n}{2}\sum_j\log(d_j) + \frac{n}{2}\log|\Omega| + \frac{n}{2}\sum_k\log(S_k)
    + \sum_j \tau_{j\cdot}\log(\alpha) - \sum_{jk}\tau_{jk}\log(\tau_{jk})$$

### 4. Unknown clusters, spherical noise (VEM)

R6: `NormalBlockVarUnknownClusters` (`noise_covariance = "spherical"`).

C++: `norm_block_var_cov_spherical_noise_unknown_clusters`.

Identical to §3 with $d_j = \xi$ for all $j$:

$$\xi^{-1} = \frac{1}{p}\sum_j \hat d_j = \frac{A_{\mathrm{total\text{-}sum}}}{np}$$

### 5. Zero-inflation extension

R6: `ZINormalBlockVarKnownClusters`, `ZINormalBlockVarUnknownClusters`. C++: `ZINormalBlockData`, `ZINormalBlockVarKnownClusters` / `ZINormalBlockVarUnknownClusters`.

$$\begin{aligned}
\text{Excess-of-zero layer:} \quad & Z_i \sim \bigotimes_j \mathrm{Bernoulli}(\kappa_j) \\
\text{Observation space:} \quad & Y_i \mid Z_i, W_i = Z_i \odot \delta_0 + (1-Z_i)\odot\big(CW_i + \mathcal N(B^\top X_i, D)\big)
\end{aligned}$$

We write $\mathbf 1_Y = \texttt{zeros\_bar}$ ($n\times p$, $1$ where $Y_{ij}\neq 0$), $\mathbf 0_Y = 1 - \mathbf 1_Y$, $nY = (\mathbf 1_Y)_{\mathrm{col\text{-}sum}}$ (per-variable count of non-zero observations), $npY = (\mathbf 1_Y)_{\mathrm{total\text{-}sum}}$.

$\kappa$ is estimated once, upfront, outside the (V)EM loop: a per-variable logistic regression of $\mathbf 0_Y[\cdot, j]$ on the zero-inflation design matrix $X_0$ (defaulting to an intercept-only column when $X_0$ is not supplied, in which case $\kappa_j$ reduces exactly to the empirical zero-proportion of variable $j$). $\kappa$ is never updated during the (V)EM recursion; only its fixed contribution to the log-likelihood,

$$\texttt{zi\_cond\_mean} = \sum\big(\mathbf 0_Y \odot \log(\kappa)\big) + \sum\big(\mathbf 1_Y \odot \log(1-\kappa)\big),$$

is carried through the C++ core (`ZINormalBlockData::zi_cond_mean`).

Throughout, $W = \mathbf 1_Y \odot D^{-1}$ (broadcast $d$ over rows, masked by $\mathbf 1_Y$) is the "masked weight" matrix used in every closed-form solve below (`dm1_mat` / `DM1` in the code).

### 6. ZI, known clusters, diagonal noise (EM)

C++: `zi_norm_block_var_cov_diag_noise_known_clusters`.

Because the zero-inflation mask varies row by row, the posterior covariance of $W_i \mid Y_i$ is **row-dependent**: $\Gamma$ is a family of $n$ distinct $q\times q$ matrices (`arma::cube`), not a single shared matrix as in §1.

**E-step.** With $R = Y - XB$ (current $B$):

$$\forall i: \quad \Gamma^{(i)} = \big(\Omega+ \mathrm{diag}((WC)_{i\cdot})\big)^{-1} \qquad [q\times q]$$

$$\forall i: \quad \mu_i = \big((R\odot W)C\big)_{i\cdot}\, \Gamma^{(i)} \qquad [q]$$

**M-step.** $B$ has no closed form *as a single linear system* (the mask makes each column's weights different), but the per-column subproblem stays exactly quadratic, hence solvable column-by-column (`nb_optim::solve_wls`, Part II):

$$\hat B = \arg\min_B \; \sum\Big( W \odot (Y - XB - \mu C^\top)^2 \Big) \qquad \text{[solved one column at a time]}$$

With $R_\mu = R - \mu C^\top$ ($R$ refreshed with the new $\hat B$ first, see Part II) and $\big(C\mathrm{diag}(\Gamma)\big)_i := C\,\mathrm{diag}(\Gamma^{(i)})$ (expansion of each row's posterior variance to the variable level via the cluster structure):

$$A = R_\mu^2 + \big(C\mathrm{diag}(\Gamma)\big)_{i\cdot} \qquad [n\times p]$$

$$\hat d = nY \oslash (\mathbf 1_Y \odot A)_{\mathrm{col\text{-}sum}}$$

$$\hat\Sigma = \frac{1}{n}\Big(\mu^\top\mu + \sum_i \Gamma^{(i)}\Big)$$

$$\hat\Omega= \hat\Sigma^{-1} \qquad \text{(or graphical lasso, §13)}$$

**Criterion** (mirrors §1's general form: one marginal per row, restricted to that row's own observed/non-zero-inflated columns, via the same Woodbury trick applied to each row's own $\Gamma^{(i),-1}$):

$$\begin{aligned}J & = -\frac{npY}{2}\log(2\pi) + \frac12 \sum_j nY_j \log(d_j) + \frac{n}{2}\log|\Omega| + \frac12 \sum_i \log|\Gamma^{(i)}|
    \\ & \qquad - \frac12\Big(\underbrace{\textstyle\sum(W\odot R^2)}_{\text{weighted SSQ}} - \textstyle\sum_i \mu_i^\top \Gamma^{(i),-1}\mu_i\Big) + \texttt{zi\_cond\_mean}.\end{aligned}$$

valid at any $(B,d,\Omega)$, for the same reason as §1. At an M-step-consistent point the bracketed term collapses to $npY$ and this reduces to

$$J = -\frac{npY}{2}\log(2\pi e) + \frac12 \sum_j nY_j \log(d_j) + \frac{n}{2}\log|\Omega|
    + \frac12 \sum_i \log|\Gamma^{(i)}| + \texttt{zi\_cond\_mean}.$$

### 7. ZI, known clusters, spherical noise (EM)

C++: `zi_norm_block_var_cov_spherical_noise_known_clusters`. Identical to §6 with:

$$\xi^{-1} = \frac{npY}{(\mathbf 1_Y \odot A)_{\mathrm{total\text{-}sum}}}$$

### 8. ZI, unknown clusters, diagonal noise (VEM)

C++: `zi_norm_block_var_cov_diag_noise_unknown_clusters`.

Same mean-field approximation as §3, but the zero-inflation mask makes the variational variance *row-dependent*: $S$ is now an $n\times q$ matrix, not a length-$q$ vector.

**VE-step.** With $R = Y - XB$:

$$M = \arg\max_M \; -\frac12 \Big( \sum\big(W\odot(M^2\tau^\top - 2R\odot(M\tau^\top))\big) + \sum\big((M\Omega)\odot M\big) \Big)$$

$$S = \big(W\tau + \mathbf 1_n \mathrm{diag}(\Omega)^\top\big)^{\oslash} \qquad [n\times q]$$

$$\eta = -\frac12\Big(W^\top(M^2+S) - 2(W\odot R)^\top M\Big) + \mathbf 1_p \log(\alpha)^\top - 1$$

$$\tau_{j\cdot} = \mathrm{softmax}(\eta_{j\cdot}) \qquad \text{(skipped if } q=1 \text{ or fixed\_tau)}$$

$M$'s objective is exactly quadratic and *row-separable* (mirrors $\Gamma^{(i)}/\mu_i$ in §6): each row solves an independent $q\times q$ ridge system (`nb_optim::solve_M_ridge`, Part II):

$$\forall i: \quad M_i = \big(\Omega+ \mathrm{diag}((WC)_{i\cdot})\big)^{-1} \big((W\odot R)C\big)_{i\cdot}$$

**M-step.** With $A = R^2 - 2R\odot(M\tau^\top) + (M^2+S)\tau^\top$ and $R$ refreshed with the new $\hat B$ before estimating $d$ (Part II):

$$\hat B = \arg\min_B \; \sum\Big( W \odot (Y - XB - M\tau^\top)^2 \Big) \qquad \text{[solved one column at a time]}$$

$$\hat d = nY \oslash (\mathbf 1_Y \odot A)_{\mathrm{col\text{-}sum}}$$

$$\hat\alpha = \mathrm{mean}_{\text{cols}}(\tau)$$

$$\hat\Sigma_q = \frac{1}{n}M^\top M + \mathrm{diag}\big(\mathrm{mean}_{\text{cols}}(S)\big)$$

$$\hat\Omega= \hat\Sigma_q^{-1} \qquad \text{(or graphical lasso, §13)}$$

**Criterion:**

$$\begin{aligned}
J &= -\frac{npY}{2}\log(2\pi e) + \frac12\sum_j nY_j\log(d_j) + \frac{n}{2}\log|\Omega| + \frac12\sum_{ik}\log(S_{ik}) \\
  &\quad + \sum_j\tau_{j\cdot}\log(\alpha) - \sum_{jk}\tau_{jk}\log(\tau_{jk}) + \texttt{zi\_cond\_mean}
\end{aligned}$$

($\sum_{ik}\log(S_{ik})$ now ranges over all $n\times q$ entries, since $S$ is row-dependent.)

### 9. ZI, unknown clusters, spherical noise (VEM)

C++: `zi_norm_block_var_cov_spherical_noise_unknown_clusters`. Identical to §8 with:

$$\xi^{-1} = \frac{npY}{(\mathbf 1_Y\odot A)_{\mathrm{total\text{-}sum}}}$$

## Mean-Block models (response clustering)

The clustering structures the *mean*: two variables are in the same block when they respond identically to the covariates, i.e. when they share a *regression profile* ($\S\S10$-11). See @ngalala2026 for the model's original derivation.

### 10. The generative model

R6: `NormalBlockMeanKnownClusters`, `NormalBlockMeanUnknownClusters` (`normal_block(..., model = "mean")`).

C++: `norm_block_mean_known_clusters`, `norm_block_mean_unknown_clusters`.

$$Y_i = C B^\top X_i + \varepsilon_i, \qquad \varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal N(0, \Sigma), \quad Y_i, \varepsilon_i \in \mathbb R^p$$

$C$ ($p\times q$) is the same clustering matrix as in §0 -- fixed 0/1, or a variational $\tau$ -- but it now multiplies the mean rather than a latent vector. $B$ is $d\times q$, *one column per cluster* (against $d\times p$, one per variable, in §§1-9): variables in the same block are constrained to respond *identically* to the covariates. In matrix form $\mathbb E[Y] = X B C^\top$. $\Sigma$ is the $p\times p$ residual covariance, $\Omega= \Sigma^{-1}$, with three possible shapes (§10.3).

The two families are complementary, not variants of one another:

|   | variance-block (§§1-9) | mean-block (§§10-11) |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| what the clustering constrains | the latent covariance | the mean response to $X$ |
| $B$ | $d\times p$, unconstrained | $d\times q$, shared within a block |
| covariance | $D$ diagonal/spherical, plus $C\Omega^{-1}C^\top$ | $\Sigma$, unconstrained up to its shape |
| latent variable | $W_i\in\mathbb R^q$ | none |
| free parameters | $pd + q + \binom q2 + |D|$ | $qd + |\Sigma|$ |

Because there is no latent variable, the known-clusters case is not an EM at all: it is block coordinate ascent on the exact log-likelihood, alternating $B$ and $\Sigma$ (the C++ `E_step()` is a deliberate no-op there). Only the unknown-clusters case needs a variational treatment, and only for $C$.

#### 10.1 Known clusters

**M-step.** Maximizing $-\tfrac12\mathrm{tr}\big((Y-XBC^\top)\Omega(Y-XBC^\top)^\top\big)$ in $B$ gives the normal equations $X^\top Y\,\Omega C = X^\top X\, B\, C^\top\Omega C$, hence

$$\hat B = (X^\top X)^{-1} X^\top Y\, \Omega\, C\, (C^\top \Omega C)^{-1} \qquad [d\times q]$$

$$R = Y - XBC^\top, \qquad \hat\Sigma = \frac1n R^\top R \qquad \text{(shape-restricted, §10.3)}$$

**Criterion** (exact log-likelihood, valid at any $(B,\Omega)$):

$$J = -\frac{np}{2}\log(2\pi) + \frac n2 \log|\Omega| - \frac12 \mathrm{tr}\big(R\,\Omega\,R^\top\big)$$

#### 10.2 Unknown clusters (VEM)

Mean-field $\mathbb P(C\mid Y)\approx\prod_j \pi(C_j)$ with $C_j\sim\mathrm{Mult}(1,\tau_{j\cdot})$ and prior $\alpha$. Write $w = \mathrm{diag}(\Omega)$ and $M = B^\top X^\top X B$ ($q\times q$).

The only quantity the mean-field introduces is $\mathbb E_q[C^\top \Omega C]$, which is *not* $\tau^\top\Omega\tau$: the diagonal blocks $\mathbb E[C_jC_j^\top] = \mathrm{Diag}(\tau_{j\cdot})$ differ from $\tau_{j\cdot}\tau_{j\cdot}^\top$. Hence

$$\Psi = \mathbb E_q[C^\top \Omega C] = \tau^\top\Omega\tau + \underbrace{\mathrm{Diag}(\tau^\top w) - \tau^\top \mathrm{Diag}(w)\,\tau}_{\textstyle \Phi} \qquad [q\times q]$$

$\Phi$ is the variance part, and is what survives in the ELBO's trace term below.

**M-step.**

$$\hat B = (X^\top X)^{-1} X^\top Y\, \Omega\, \tau\, \Psi^{-1}$$

$$\bar R = Y - XB\tau^\top, \qquad
\Lambda = \mathrm{Diag}(\lambda), \quad
\lambda_j = \frac{\tau_{j\cdot}^\top\mathrm{diag}(M) - \tau_{j\cdot}^\top M \tau_{j\cdot}}{n}$$

$$\hat\Sigma = \frac1n \bar R^\top \bar R + \Lambda \qquad \text{(shape-restricted, §10.3)}, \qquad
\hat\alpha = \frac1p \tau_{\mathrm{col\text{-}sum}}$$

$\Lambda$ is the variational correction: $\mathbb E_q\|Y_i - CB^\top X_i\|^2$ exceeds the plug-in residual $\bar R$ by exactly the within-row variance of the cluster assignment.

**VE-step.** Each row of $\tau$ has a closed-form softmax; with $G = Y^\top X B - \tau M$,

$$\eta_{jk} = \log\alpha_k + (\Omega_{j\cdot} G)_k + w_j\,(\tau_{j\cdot}^\top M)_k - \tfrac12 w_j M_{kk},
\qquad \tau_{j\cdot} = \mathrm{softmax}(\eta_{j\cdot})$$

The rows are swept sequentially (Gauss-Seidel), $G$ being refreshed after each: see Part II, which explains why updating them simultaneously is not merely slower but can cycle.

**ELBO.**

$$J = -\frac{np}{2}\log(2\pi) + \frac n2\log|\Omega|
  + \sum_{jk}\tau_{jk}\log\alpha_k - \sum_{jk}\tau_{jk}\log\tau_{jk}
  - \frac12\Big(\mathrm{tr}(\bar R\,\Omega\,\bar R^\top) + \mathrm{tr}(\Phi M)\Big)$$

#### 10.3 The shape of $\Sigma$

$\Sigma$ is $p\times p$ here, not $q\times q$, so its shape is a modelling decision rather than a detail. Writing $S = \tfrac1n\bar R^\top\bar R + \Lambda$ (or $\tfrac1n R^\top R$ for known clusters):

| `noise_covariance` | $\hat\Omega$ | free parameters |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| `"full"` | $S^{-1}$, or the graphical lasso of §13 | $p + \binom p2$ |
| `"diagonal"` (default) | $\mathrm{Diag}(1 \oslash \mathrm{diag}(S))$ | $p$ |
| `"spherical"` | $\mathrm{Diag}\big(1/\overline{\mathrm{diag}(S)}\big)$ | $1$ |

`"diagonal"` is the default, for a statistical reason rather than a computational one: a full $\Sigma$ spends $p(p+1)/2$ parameters that drown the mean structure BIC/ICL are asked to weigh, and it selects $q$ worse as $p$ approaches $n$, even when the data were generated with a full $\Sigma$. Clustering quality at fixed $q$ is the same either way; what a full $\Sigma$ costs is the choice of $q$. It becomes competitive at a comfortable $n/p$, where the covariance is well estimated.

Two consequences of the restricted shapes: they never invert anything, so unlike `"full"` they carry no $n > p$ requirement; and with $\Omega$ diagonal, $\Psi$ collapses to $\mathrm{Diag}(\tau^\top w)$ and the $\tau$-dependence in $\eta$ above cancels, making the VE-step a genuine one-shot softmax. Asking for `sparsity > 0` implies `"full"`: there are no off-diagonal terms for the graphical lasso to penalize otherwise.

### 11. Zero-inflated mean-block

R6: `ZINormalBlockMeanKnownClusters`, `ZINormalBlockMeanUnknownClusters`. C++: `zi_norm_block_mean_known_clusters`, `zi_norm_block_mean_unknown_clusters`.

Same excess-of-zero layer as §5, same $\kappa$ estimated once upfront, same fixed `zi_cond_mean` contribution. Restricted to `"diagonal"` and `"spherical"` $\Sigma$, and for a structural reason: a full $\Sigma$ ties the variables together within each row, and the mask leaves a *different* set of them observed in every row, so each row would need its own $p_i\times p_i$ submatrix inverse -- a missing-data EM rather than a reweighting.

With $\Sigma$ diagonal the Gaussian part factorizes over $(i,j)$ and the mask is simply a $0/1$ weight. Writing $w$ for the precision vector, $Z = XB$ ($n\times q$), $T$ for the membership matrix ($C$ if known, $\tau$ if not), and $\mathbf 1_Y$ as in §5, everything the recursion needs is carried by two $p\times q$ statistics:

$$A_{jk} = \sum_i (\mathbf 1_Y)_{ij} Z_{ik}^2, \qquad
  P_{jk} = \sum_i (\mathbf 1_Y)_{ij} Y_{ij} Z_{ik}, \qquad
  \mathrm{ssq}_j = \sum_i (\mathbf 1_Y)_{ij} Y_{ij}^2$$

$$s_j \;=\; \mathbb E_T\Big[\sum_i (\mathbf 1_Y)_{ij}\,(Y_{ij}-Z_{i,c_j})^2\Big]
   \;=\; \mathrm{ssq}_j - 2\sum_k T_{jk}P_{jk} + \sum_k T_{jk}A_{jk}$$

No $p\times p$ matrix is ever formed, and no separate $\Lambda$ is needed: the variational variance is already inside the $T$-weighted $A$ term.

**M-step.** The $B$-update loses the single closed form of §10.1. The weight of observation $i$ for cluster $k$, $a_{ik} = \sum_j (\mathbf 1_Y)_{ij} w_j T_{jk}$, now depends on $i$, so the one $(X^\top X)^{-1}$ solve splits into $q$ weighted least squares in dimension $d$:

$$\hat\beta_k = \big(X^\top \mathrm{Diag}(a_{\cdot k}) X\big)^{-1} X^\top b_{\cdot k},
\qquad b_{ik} = \sum_j (\mathbf 1_Y)_{ij}\, w_j\, Y_{ij}\, T_{jk}$$

$$\hat w_j = \frac{nY_j}{s_j} \quad \text{(diagonal)}, \qquad
  \hat w = \frac{npY}{\sum_j s_j} \quad \text{(spherical)}, \qquad
  \hat\alpha = \frac1p \tau_{\mathrm{col\text{-}sum}}$$

**VE-step** (unknown clusters). The ELBO is linear in each row of $\tau$ up to the entropy, and the rows are independent, so the softmax is the exact maximizer in one shot: no sweep, unlike §10.2, whose full $\Sigma$ couples the rows:

$$\tau_{jk} \propto \alpha_k \exp\Big(w_j\big(P_{jk} - \tfrac12 A_{jk}\big)\Big)$$

**Criterion.**

$$J = -\frac{npY}{2}\log(2\pi) + \frac12\sum_j nY_j\log(w_j) - \frac12\sum_j w_j s_j + \texttt{zi\_cond\_mean}$$

plus $\sum_{jk}\tau_{jk}\log\alpha_k - \sum_{jk}\tau_{jk}\log\tau_{jk}$ for unknown clusters.

As a check on the mask handling: on data with no zeros at all, $\kappa = 0$, `zi_cond_mean` $=0$, and these reduce exactly to §10 -- verified numerically to $10^{-5}$ in `tests/testthat/test-ZINormalBlockMean*.R`.

## Combining both families

The two remaining topics apply across both families rather than to one: chaining them (\S12), and the sparsity penalty (\S13) shared by every variant that carries a full precision matrix to regularize (\S\S1-9's cluster-level $\Omega$, \S10's variable-level one under `noise_covariance = "full"`).

### 12. Sequential mean-then-variance fits

`normal_block_sequential()` fits the two families one after the other: a mean-block model on $Y$, then a variance-block model on its residuals with an intercept-only design (the covariate effects having been removed by the first stage). This is a heuristic two-stage estimator, not a joint model.

On data carrying two distinct structures it recovers both. On real data the two partitions are typically unrelated, so a joint model forcing them equal would be misspecified, while the covariance clustering changes little when the mean structure is removed first: the two structures look *separable* rather than competing. A joint mean+covariance model, with free or linked partitions, remains open.

### 13. Sparse precision matrix (graphical lasso)

In every variant above, whenever `sparsity` $>0$, $\hat\Omega$ is no longer the exact inverse of $\hat\Sigma$ (or $\hat\Sigma_q$): it is estimated by the graphical lasso (`src/graphical_lasso.h`, reached through `nb_omega::estimate()` in `src/omega_estimation.h`) applied to $\hat\Sigma$ with penalty $\lambda \odot W_\lambda$ ($W_\lambda$ a $q\times q$ matrix of per-pair weights, `sparsity_weights`, diagonal excluded from the penalty, and $\lambda$ the scalar `sparsity`).

For the **known-clusters criteria (§1, §2, §6, §7)**, this needs no special case at all: the general formula given there is $\log p(Y;\theta)$ for *any* symmetric positive-definite $\Omega$, sparse or not -- it never assumes $\hat\Omega$ is $\hat\Sigma$'s exact inverse, so no correction term is added when $\lambda>0$.

For the **unknown-clusters criteria (§3, §4, §8, §9)**, which still use the profiled (M-step-only) ELBO form, $\hat\Omega$ no longer satisfies $\mathrm{tr}(\hat\Omega\hat\Sigma) = q$ there (the identity that makes the corresponding term collapse to a constant when the inversion is exact), so those four criteria gain an explicit correction term when $\lambda > 0$:

$$J_{\text{struct}} = J + \frac{nq}{2} - \frac{n}{2}\,\mathrm{tr}(\hat\Omega\hat\Sigma) - \lambda \sum\big|W_\lambda \odot \hat\Omega\big|$$

where $\hat\Sigma$ is the corresponding M-step covariance estimate of each variant. This is implemented identically (modulo the variant-specific $\hat\Sigma$) in `NormalBlockVarUnknownClusters` and `ZINormalBlockVarUnknownClusters`'s `objective()`.

The **mean-block unknown-clusters criterion (§10.2)** needs no such correction, for a different reason than the known-clusters case above: it is not a profiled shortcut to begin with. Its ELBO (the formula in §10.2) is written out in full from $(B,\Omega)$ -- via $\log|\Omega|$ and the trace terms $\mathrm{tr}(\bar R\,\Omega\,\bar R^\top) + \mathrm{tr}(\Phi M)$ -- and never assumes $\Omega=\hat\Sigma^{-1}$ at any point, sparse or not; the penalty term is simply subtracted from it directly (`NormalBlockMeanUnknownClusters::objective()`, `src/normal_block_mean_unknown_clusters.h`).

**Choosing the penalty.** Along a sparsity path (`sparsity = TRUE`), $\lambda$ is chosen by BIC, EBIC or ICL (below), or by StARS (Liu, Roeder & Wasserman, 2010) through `get_best_model("StARS")`, for both families (`NormalBlockCollectionSparsity`). StARS refits the whole path on subsamples of the observations -- 10 by default, of size $10\sqrt n$ if $n\ge144$ and $0.8n$ otherwise -- with the clustering held fixed so that the networks are comparable across subsamples: the known one; for a variance-block model with unknown clusters, the variational $\tau$ of the least penalized model with `fixed_tau = TRUE`; for a mean-block model, the MAP partition of the least penalized model, refitted as a known clustering (its network relates the $p$ variables, so its edges do not depend on cluster labels). Each subsample path reuses the collection's penalties. The stability at $\lambda$ is $1-\overline{4\hat p_e(1-\hat p_e)}$ over the edges $e$, $\hat p_e$ the edge's selection frequency, and the selected $\lambda$ is the smallest one whose stability reaches the requested level (0.9 by default).

### Model-selection criteria

Every variant reports the same three criteria (`R/NormalBlockBase.R`), on the deviance scale (lower is better), from $J$ the criterion of its section above: the exact log-likelihood for known clusters (§1-2, §6-7, §10.1, §11), and also for the mean-block family with a diagonal or spherical $\Sigma$ even when the clusters are unknown -- the columns of $Y$ are then independent given $C$, so the mean-field posterior over $C$ is exact and the VEM is a genuine EM -- and the ELBO otherwise (§3-4, §8-9, §10.2 with a full $\Sigma$).

**BIC: one penalty per group of parameters.** Following the ICL of @daudin2008mixture for stochastic block models and of @keribin2015lbm for latent block models, a group of $\nu_g$ free parameters is charged $\nu_g\log N_g$, with $N_g$ the number of independent observations informing it rather than $n$ throughout:

$$\mathrm{BIC} = -2J + \sum_g \nu_g \log N_g .$$

| group | variance-block $\nu_g$ | mean-block $\nu_g$ | $N_g$ |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| cluster proportions $\alpha$ (unknown clusters) | $q-1$ | $q-1$ | $p$ |
| variable-specific regression coefficients | $pd$ | -- | $n$ |
| cluster profiles $\beta_k$ (columns of $B$) | -- | $qd$ | $np$ |
| diagonal noise $d_j$ / $w_j$ | $p$ | $p$ | $n$ |
| spherical noise | $1$ | $1$ | $np$ |
| precision matrix: diagonal + non-zero off-diagonal terms | $q + \lvert E\rvert$ | $p + \lvert E\rvert$ (full $\Sigma$) | $n$ |
| zero-inflation coefficients $\kappa$ | $p\,d_0$ | $p\,d_0$ | $n$ |

The variables are the units being clustered, hence $\log p$ for $\alpha$; a cluster profile $\beta_k$ is shared by all the $n\times p_k$ cells of its block, hence the $\log(np)$ of a latent block model's block parameters, and the same holds for a spherical variance. `penalty_terms` returns this table for a fitted model, `penalty` its total and `nb_param` $=\sum_g\nu_g$ (the `df` of `logLik()`).

**ICL: the partition alone is completed.** As in @biernacki2000icl, the ICL completes the discrete clustering only, the latent vectors $W$ of the variance-block family being integrated out: since $\mathbb E_\tau[\log p(Y,C)] \ge J - \mathcal H(\tau)$ (§3's ELBO splits as an expected complete log-likelihood in $(W,C)$ plus the entropies of $W$ and of $C$),

$$\mathrm{ICL} = \mathrm{BIC} + 2\,\mathcal H(\tau), \qquad \mathcal H(\tau) = -\sum_{jk}\tau_{jk}\log\tau_{jk},$$

so that $\mathrm{ICL} = \mathrm{BIC}$ for a known clustering. Completing $W$ as well (adding its Gaussian entropy) would make the ICL differ from the BIC even for known clusters, and depend on the scale of the data.

**EBIC.** The extended BIC of @foygel2010ebic with $\gamma = 1/2$, on the network the sparsity acts on:

$$\mathrm{EBIC} = \mathrm{BIC} + 2\,\lvert E\rvert \log(\mathrm{dim}), \qquad \mathrm{dim} = q \ \text{(variance-block)}, \quad p \ \text{(mean-block, full } \Sigma).$$

**Open point.** Under `sparsity > 0`, $\lvert E\rvert$ counts the non-zero off-diagonal terms of $\hat\Omega$ (the degrees of freedom of the lasso). For the mean-block family with a full $\Sigma$ this makes the BIC non-monotone in $q$ whenever a larger $q$ leaves $\hat\Omega$ sparser; the diagonal default is unaffected.

**Held-out log-likelihood and cross-validation.** `heldout_loglik(newdata)` evaluates new observations at the fitted parameters and, for an unknown clustering, at the MAP partition $\tilde C$; the rows are then independent and each one's log-likelihood is exact. For the variance-block family, $Y_i \sim \mathcal N(B^\top X_i,\ \tilde C\Sigma\tilde C^\top + D)$, evaluated with $A = \Omega + \tilde C^\top D^{-1}\tilde C$ ($q\times q$, diagonal second term since $\tilde C$ is a partition):
$$\log\lvert \tilde C\Sigma\tilde C^\top + D\rvert = \log\lvert D\rvert - \log\lvert\Omega\rvert + \log\lvert A\rvert, \qquad r^\top(\tilde C\Sigma\tilde C^\top + D)^{-1}r = r^\top D^{-1}r - u^\top A^{-1}u,\quad u = \tilde C^\top D^{-1} r.$$
Zero-inflated variants add $\sum_{j:\,y_{ij}=0}\log\kappa_{ij} + \sum_{j:\,y_{ij}\neq0}\log(1-\kappa_{ij})$, with $\kappa$ from the new $X^0$, and apply the same formulas to the non-zero sub-row. The mean-block family is Gaussian with precision $\Omega$ directly. Values are on $Y$'s original scale ($-n\sum_j\log s_j$ for a rescaled fit). With a known clustering, on the training data, this is the model's log-likelihood. `normal_block_cv()` sums it over $K$ folds of observations, re-estimating everything (clustering included) on each training set; since superfluous clusters barely hurt prediction, it plateaus beyond the true $q$, and the reported choice follows the one-standard-error rule.

# Part II -- Implementation and numerical notes

Nothing in this part changes any model of Part I. It records how the formulas are evaluated, which shortcuts are exact, and the safeguards the implementation relies on. All initialization is done in R (the R6 classes); each C++ class runs the (V)EM recursion from the parameters passed in, through one `*_fit` entry point (`src/exports.cpp`).

## 14. Correctness invariants of the recursion

- **The residual** $R = Y - XB$ is refreshed after every update of $B$: each $d$/`dm1` update (§§1-4, 6-9) uses the residual of the *current* $B$.
- **`objective()` recomputes everything from** $(B, d, \Omega)$ (plus the variational parameters), and reads back nothing cached by the preceding E-step, except $XB$ (§16). The known-clusters criteria (§1, §2, §6, §7) are therefore the marginal log-likelihood at *any* $\theta$, which the SQUAREM acceptance test (§18) requires.

## 15. Closed-form updates

- **No iterative optimizer is used.** The zero-inflation mask only reweights the residuals, so the ZI updates of $B$ and $M$ stay quadratic: one weighted least-squares solve per column of $B$ (`nb_optim::solve_wls`) and one $q\times q$ ridge solve per row of $M$ (`nb_optim::solve_M_ridge`), in `src/zi_closed_form_solvers.h`. The R-side initialization of $B$ (`zi_weighted_fit()`, `R/utils.R`) solves the same weighted least squares.
- **The per-row and per-column systems are solved as SPD systems.** $\Omega$ is positive definite and the diagonal added to it non-negative, so these many small systems use Armadillo's SPD path (`solve_opts::likely_sympd`, with a guarded fallback) and a reused buffer: at these sizes the cost is the per-call overhead, not the arithmetic. The mean-block update of $B$ likewise solves with $\Psi$ rather than inverting it.
- **The mean-block VE-step sweeps the rows of** $\tau$ sequentially. Each row's softmax (§10.2) maximizes the ELBO exactly in that row, so a sweep refreshing $G$ after each row is a coordinate ascent and cannot decrease the ELBO; updating all rows at once from the same $G$ can cycle. With $\Omega$ diagonal the coupling cancels and one softmax suffices, which is why the zero-inflated variant (§11) needs no sweep.

## 16. Numerical safeguards

- **Singular weighted normal equations are expected.** With a one-hot design and zero-inflated data, a design level can have no non-zero observation for some variable: both sides of its weighted normal equations vanish on that coordinate. `arma::solve()` then falls back to the minimum-norm solution (its warning is silenced by `-DARMA_WARN_LEVEL=1` in `src/Makevars`), and `zi_weighted_fit()` uses `MASS::ginv()` to the same effect. A variable fitted exactly by $\hat B$ would get an infinite precision: the weighted residual sum of squares is floored away from 0.
- **$XB$ is cached** and invalidated only when $B$ changes, which goes through `set_B()`, `set_state()` or `copy_tracked_state_from()`; every E-step, M-step and objective needs $Y - XB$, often for the same $B$.
- In the zero-inflated variants, the masked weight matrix computed in `E_step()` is reused by `M_step()`.

## 17. The graphical lasso solver

The penalized $\hat\Omega$ of §13 is computed by an in-package solver (`src/graphical_lasso.h`, shared verbatim with PLNmodels, reached through `nb_omega::estimate()` in `src/omega_estimation.h`): the block coordinate descent of @friedman2008sparse, in the bookkeeping of @sustik2012glassofast. Running it in C++ keeps the whole (V)EM inside a single `.Call`, with no callback into R.

- **Scaled problem.** It is solved for the covariance scaled to a unit diagonal, an exact change of variables that keeps the descent stable when the variances span orders of magnitude; an indefinite result is shifted on its diagonal, which keeps its support.
- **Degenerate inputs.** With no off-diagonal mass (in particular $q = 1$) the solution is the diagonal $1/(S_{ii} + \rho_{ii})$, returned directly; non-finite input and non-positive $S_{ii}+\rho_{ii}$ are rejected up front.
- **Warm starts.** Consecutive M-steps solve nearly the same problem, so each one resumes from the previous solution, at a tight threshold (`nb_omega::kGlassoThreshold`, mirrored by `NB_GLASSO_THRESHOLD` in R for the reference recursions): fewer sweeps and a more accurate solution than cold starts at a looser threshold. A warm start can diverge on an ill-conditioned $\hat\Sigma$; `nb_omega::estimate()` then retries cold, and only if that fails too falls back to the unpenalized inverse.

## 18. SQUAREM: a generic accelerator wrapped around (V)EM

**Principle.** A (V)EM recursion is a fixed-point iteration $\theta_{t+1} = T(\theta_t)$, $T$ being one E-step + M-step (or VE-step + M-step) cycle, guaranteed to increase the objective $J$ but not to do so fast: when the largest eigenvalue of $T$'s Jacobian at the fixed point is close to 1, which happens as $q$ grows here, plain (V)EM crawls. SQUAREM [@varadhan2008squarem] is a generic fixed-point acceleration: from two successive applications of $T$, it extrapolates a longer step, then applies $T$ once more to stabilize it. It only calls the model's own $T$.

**Pseudo-code** (one outer iteration, `try_squarem_step()` in `src/normal_block_em_base.h`):

``` text
Input: theta_0 (current iterate), T (one E/M or VE/M cycle), objective J
theta_1 <- T(theta_0)
theta_2 <- T(theta_1)           # two plain (V)EM steps, as usual

r <- theta_1 - theta_0
v <- (theta_2 - theta_1) - r
if ||v|| is ~0: return theta_2  # no curvature to extrapolate from -> plain EM

alpha <- -||r|| / ||v||         # alpha <= -1; alpha = -1 <=> no extrapolation

repeat up to 10 times:          # SQUAREM's quadratic extrapolation
    theta_star  <- theta_0 - 2*alpha*r + alpha^2*v
    if theta_star is feasible:
        theta_new <- T(theta_star) # one stabilizing (V)EM cycle
        if J(theta_new) >= J(theta_2):
            return theta_new    # accept
    alpha <- (alpha - 1) / 2    # backtrack towards alpha = -1
return theta_2                  # every attempt rejected: plain (V)EM
```

It degenerates exactly to two ordinary (V)EM steps when every extrapolation is rejected, and an accepted candidate is itself the image of a (V)EM cycle that does at least as well as $\theta_2$: it never does worse than plain (V)EM. Only the parameters with a closed-form M-step are extrapolated, $\theta = (B, d, \Omega)$ for the variance-block family and $\theta = (B, \Omega)$ for the mean-block one; the variational and posterior parameters are only refreshed by the E-step inside $T$.

**The acceptance test.** For the known-clusters criteria (§1, §2, §6, §7) `objective()` is the marginal log-likelihood at any $\theta$ (§14). For the unknown-clusters criteria (§3, §4, §8, §9) it is the profiled ELBO, which is valid right after a VE-step + M-step pair -- exactly where every comparison takes place.

**When it runs** (`NB_control(acceleration = )`, passed as `accelerate` to every `*_fit` entry point). By default, for the variance-block family, where plain VEM may not converge within the iteration cap at large $q$, and for mean-block models with a full $\Sigma$; not for mean-block models with a diagonal or spherical $\Sigma$, whose EM is exact and converges in a few dozen iterations, so that rejected extrapolations only cost time. `TRUE` or `FALSE` forces it. It is never used when `sparsity > 0`: the graphical lasso is an iterative, approximate M-step, and extrapolating amplifies its small non-monotonicities for little gain.

**Code map** (landscape table below; the variance-block rows omit the common prefix of their C++ aliases, `norm_block_var_cov_` or `zi_norm_block_var_cov_`). Both noise shapes of a variance-block variant share one C++ template, parameterized by a `NoisePolicy` (`DiagonalNoise`/`SphericalNoise`, `ZIDiagonalNoise`/`ZISphericalNoise`), which only changes the $d$/$\xi$ update. The mean-block classes take `noise_covariance` as a runtime argument, since it only changes how $\hat\Omega$ is computed from the residuals (`omega_from_residuals()`).

Both noise variants of a given clustering mode share one C++ template, parameterized by `NoisePolicy` (`NormalBlockVarKnownClusters`, `NormalBlockVarUnknownClusters`, `ZINormalBlockVarKnownClusters`, `ZINormalBlockVarUnknownClusters`), instantiated with `DiagonalNoise`/`SphericalNoise` or `ZIDiagonalNoise`/`ZISphericalNoise`; only the $d$/$\xi$ update differs between the two. The Mean-Block classes (`NormalBlockMeanKnownClusters`, `NormalBlockMeanUnknownClusters`, and their ZI counterparts) are not templated this way: `cov_structure` (`"diagonal"`/`"spherical"`/`"full"`, §10.3) is a constructor argument checked at runtime, since it only changes how $\hat\Omega$ is computed from the residuals (`omega_from_residuals()`), not the shape of the recursion itself.

## 19. Initialization and what a collection shares

- **Initial clustering** (§§3-4, 8-9, 10.2, 11). A registry of heuristics (`private$clustering_methods`, `R/NormalBlockBase.R`), run once on the OLS (or masked least-squares) residuals for the variance-block family and on the fitted mean trajectories $X\widehat B$ for the mean-block family, supplies the starting $\tau$: `kmeans` on the columns; `ward2`, Ward.D2 on $1 - \mathrm{cor}(R)$; `sbm`, a Gaussian SBM on $\mathrm{cov}(R)$; `spectral`, $k$-means on the row-normalized leading eigenvectors of $\mathrm{cov}(R)$, capped at its numerical rank (for the mean-block family $X\widehat B$ has rank at most $d$, and eigenvectors beyond the rank are arbitrary). `NB_control(clustering_init = )` selects one, or takes an explicit clustering (one per $q$ for a collection), or `"best_of_inits"` to try several and keep the best fit. A heuristic that returns fewer than $q$ groups falls back to `ward2`.
- **Default: `kmeans` followed by `refine()`, for both families.** For the mean-block family, `kmeans` reaches better optima than the other heuristics on real and simulated data. For the variance-block family the heuristics are equivalent on simulated data and `kmeans` + `refine()` is the best or close to it on real data; a cold-started `kmeans` collection is less stable across $q$ than a `ward2` one, which is what `refine()` repairs. `ward2` remains a good choice for zero-inflated abundances.
- **A collection computes the $q$-independent part of a heuristic once** (`clustering_path_for_family()`, `R/utils.R`): one tree cut at every $q$ for `ward2`, one eigendecomposition for `spectral`, one lossless compression of the rows for `kmeans` (`compress_columns()`, exact since it preserves the distances between columns, all $k$-means sees), and a single SBM exploration over the whole range of $q$ for `sbm`. So are the least-squares fits and the zero-inflation regressions (`NormalBlockData`). A $q$ for which the shared computation does not give exactly $q$ groups goes back to the model's own heuristic.
- **Rescaling $Y$ depends on the family.** `NormalBlockData$new(scale = NULL)` is resolved when a model is fitted (`for_family()`): variance-block models divide each column of $Y$ by its standard deviation, mean-block models do not; `TRUE` or `FALSE` forces either. Columns are never centered, the intercept absorbing each variable's mean. The variance-block model loads every variable of a block on $W_k$ with the same weight, and rescaling evens out the amplitudes with which same-block variables carry that signal on real data. The mean-block model shares a mean profile $X\beta_k$ within a block, which a per-variable rescaling breaks. Criteria and `logLik()` are computed on the scale of the fit; `heldout_loglik()` is on $Y$'s original scale. The extractors give per-variable quantities ($B$ and fitted values of the variance-block family, $\Sigma$ of the mean-block family) on the original scale; quantities shared by a cluster stay on the scale of the fit, since the scaling factors differ within a block.
- **`refine()`: a local search over a whole collection** (`NormalBlockCollectionClusters$refine()`, run by default after `optimize()`, `NB_control(refine = )`). Every model of a collection is cold-started independently, and can land in a poorer local optimum than its neighbours; the models being nested, a deviance that increases with $q$ is the visible symptom (`deviance_violations`). For every $q$, `refine()` tries splitting a cluster of the model at $q-1$ and merging two clusters of the model at $q+1$, scores the candidates by a few (V)EM iterations, fully optimizes the best ones, and keeps a candidate only if it lowers the deviance. A merge averages the two clusters' parameters; pairs are ranked by the signed correlation of their latent signals for the variance-block family (a block can only gather positively co-varying variables) and by the distance between their profiles $\beta_k$ for the mean-block family. A split divides a cluster by a 2-means on its members' residuals (variance-block) or least-squares trajectories (mean-block), `split_rule = "kmeans"`, or at the median of their noise variances, `"noise"`. The default is `"kmeans"` for the variance-block family, where it is clearly better, and `"noise"` for the mean-block family, where the two rules are close.

# References
